context: Tests whether the agent follows skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md without the task naming its scripts, flags or steps: ask only idle/done workers with standup-ask.sh and wait with standup-wait.sh, fill working/blocked rows from the round log, render with the exact uv run invocation and an explicit --now, relay the block verbatim with jq -r .block, and treat standup-wait.sh exit 5 as a terminal provider refusal.

checklist.name: uv run prefix
checklist.description: standup-plan.sh invokes standup-render.py through a command that starts with `uv run --no-project --no-python-downloads --python`. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 5

checklist.name: Python version flag
checklist.description: That uv run invocation passes `--python ">=3.11"` (or `--python '>=3.11'`) before the `python` subcommand. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 5

checklist.name: --now flag present
checklist.description: The standup-render.py call passes `--now` with an ISO-8601 timestamp: a literal, or a value the script computes and passes explicitly (e.g. from `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`). Omitting --now, or passing an unset variable, fails. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 5 '--now is required and never defaults to the clock'

checklist.name: jq -r .block for output
checklist.description: standup-plan.sh saves the renderer's JSON output to a file and prints the block with `jq -r .block <file>`, with no reformatting. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 6 'Print block from the saved output verbatim (jq -r .block <file>)'

checklist.name: Alice asked via standup-ask.sh
checklist.description: standup-plan.sh calls standup-ask.sh for alice (the idle worker) with an absolute report path, and waits on her with standup-wait.sh. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Steps 2-3

checklist.name: Bob not asked
checklist.description: standup-plan.sh does NOT call standup-ask.sh or standup-wait.sh, or send any message, to bob (state `working`). Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 1 '`working` or `blocked` — never asked'

checklist.name: Charlie not asked
checklist.description: standup-plan.sh does NOT call standup-ask.sh or standup-wait.sh, or send any message, to charlie (state `blocked`). Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 1 '`working` or `blocked` — never asked'

checklist.name: Round log used for bob/charlie
checklist.description: bob's and charlie's rows (the --extra JSON) take their done/plan/blocked content from round-log.json — read from it in the script or copied from it — not from a pane read or an invented summary. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 4 'Take the content from the round log or the assignment ledger — never from a pane read, and never from a guess'

checklist.name: Exit 5 — no retry
checklist.description: NOTES.md states that standup-wait.sh exit 5 means a confirmed provider refusal, that the worker's row is recorded as missing and the operator notified, and that the script does NOT retry, rephrase, switch models/providers, or synthesize an answer. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 3 'Exit 5 ... never automatically retry, rephrase, switch models/providers, or synthesize an answer'

checklist.name: Working/blocked explanation
checklist.description: NOTES.md explains that bob and charlie are not asked because they are working/blocked (a standup never interrupts a worker), and that their rows come from the round log. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md preamble 'A worker that is mid-task keeps working and its row comes from what you already know' and Step 1

checklist.name: Other wait outcomes handled
checklist.description: standup-plan.sh or NOTES.md handles every other standup-wait.sh outcome for alice without the script aborting: exit 1 (no answer in time) moves her row to the --extra/missing path, exit 3 (a dialog is up) relays it and leaves her to the operator, and exit 4 (answer file without the pane marker) takes the documented re-check. A script that dies under `set -e` on any of these scores 0. Source: skills/herdr-standup/SKILL.md Step 3
